title: Cenote Chempita - Sprouse et al. 2015
credits: Cenote Chempita, Cedral, Cozumel, Quintana Roo; surveyed 22 June 2015 by Fernando Hernández, Steven Rehbein, Peter Sprouse and German Yañez; drawn by Peter Sprouse and German Yañez (AMCS Activities Newsletter 39, p. 17, 2016). Length 431 m, depth 45 m.
sistemaWhy: The database's cave 'Chen Pita - Rancho Juvencio El Cedral' (-KPZkVGYuc1EDzJCesO2, Gerrard 2015, no position) is this cenote, but it is filed under the sistema Purificación (-KPZgfxjlCS7yg3_43sV, aka Aerolito de Paraíso / Cueva Aerolito, 6103 m), whose Aerolito cave is on the west coast near San Miguel, about 13 km NNW of Chempita: very unlikely to be one system, so the map is not attached to it. To decide by the user: a sistema of its own for Cenote Chempita (431 m, 45 m deep, the sump 'goes 750 m plus'), or Purificación if Gerrard's grouping is confirmed.
wetDry: Mostly underwater: a lake room (pale blue, about 89% of the plan's area) under a roof, with an open collapse (drip line of T ticks) holding a dry breakdown slope (white, stippled, with a grey path down it to the water) on the west side, the 'Entrada'. A small darker blue square on the SE wall marks the sump, which the map says 'goes 750 m plus' - that passage is NOT drawn, only its mouth; the 45 m depth is in the sump.

walls.why: the lake room's walls (dashed on the east side, where unsurveyed or at a distance), the pillars in the lake (the long ticked one in the north, small ones in the east) and the boulders/pillars on the south-west wall

notWalls: width 0.24 black: the dry slope's water's edge, floor detail (boulders, the drip line's T ticks), the cross-section west of the cave and its leader, the 'L' tick by the sump; 0.24 dark grey: stipple dots on the slope; 0.12: the wavy lines in the small northern bay and the grey path (fill 0.8 grey) down the slope; 0.336: scale bar; 1.921: page frame. Blue fills: the lake (pale) and the sump mouth (darker, (0, 0.82, 0.83)).

entrances.why: the open collapse inside the drip line, with the dry breakdown slope labelled 'Entrada' - the map's only opening. Database cave 'Chen Pita - Rancho Juvencio El Cedral' (Gerrard 2015, no position, not flagged cenoteEntrance).

symbols.why: Vector map: the labels are real PDF text (page.get_text), positions in PDF points. build_layer.py doesn't read symbols yet. No depth numbers on the plan (only 'Profundidad: 45 m' in the title), no ceiling heights, no bones (no legend, no bone icon or word), no flow arrows.

northWhy: The arrow is labelled 'N cuadrícula' (grid north) and is vertical.
unverified: No trusted position: the database cave Chen Pita has none (the database's 'Rancho Juvencio El Cedral', Cave and Karst Studies, 20.35556 N 86.99861 W, is about 3 km west of this site and isn't shown to be this cenote). The control point is a best guess, not checked: a dark, NE-SW elongated opening in the canopy (about 12 x 7 m, Mapbox/Maxar imagery) just east of a palapa and a cleared yard at the end of OpenStreetMap's track 'Camino a cenote Chempita', put on the open water between the entrance slope and the drip line. OpenStreetMap's 'Cenote Chempita' node (8626714836, 20.358047 N 86.969713 W, mapped 2021 by a local mapper, changeset comment 'Surveyor', clicked on Bing imagery) is about 29 m WNW of it, so the site is right within a few tens of metres, but the fit (one point, grid north and scale bar from the map) can't be checked: the placed walls run over the palapa. To fix: a field GPS of the entrance slope and of the far (north) end of the lake.

controlPoints.name: GUESSED: the open water of the collapse, east of the entrance slope, on the dark canopy opening east of the palapa (see 'unverified')
